A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RealPC and TOPODGnet study. All 16 pages of each, including the five-page supplementary material, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses in Table 1, completion benchmarks in Table 2, and experiments with topology regularization in Table 3, supplemented by qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original dataset analyses, benchmark results, topology-regularization experiments, and supplementary qualitative evidence.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction procedure and TOPODGnet method are unchanged, including the ODGNet backbone, multilevel decoder seeds, and 0-dimensional persistent-homology regularization.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RealPC coverage of approximately 40,000 pairs across 21 categories and the same PCN/ShapeNet comparisons. The incompleteness and uniform/non-uniform sparsity scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same nine baseline rows, and Table 3 retains the comparison of ODGNet with and without topology regularization. The added reference is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The data-processing procedures, four-class dataset comparisons, Chamfer-distance metrics, and reported training settings are unchanged. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The topology on/off comparison in Table 3, qualitative analyses in Figures 5, 7, and 8, and supplementary examples and persistence diagrams in Tables 4–7 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The standard deviation used to define the non-uniformity metric is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, both Table 3 versions report CD-L1/CD-L2 values of 112.6/87.3 for ODGNet and 103.6/80.1 with topology regularization.

T1.justification: The persistent-homology definitions, filtration explanations, and loss equations in the main text and supplement are unchanged. The new figure citations do not alter mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about RealPC, limitations of existing completion methods on real-world data, and the potential of homology-based priors.

C2.justification: Interpretations involving noise, non-uniformity, topological complexity, and sensor variation are unchanged. Both versions retain the discussion of persistent-homology computation costs and the remaining noise in completion outputs.

D1.justification: Section 10 retains the NVIDIA A100 hardware disclosure and reuse of ODGNet parameters and structure. Dataset-processing instructions, manual selection of k, and the planned code/data release statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Moor et al., Topological Autoencoders (2020), as reference [33], cited in Figures 2 and 9. All earlier works remain; the broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Citation numbering and the arXiv version/date annotation change. Apart from the inserted figure citations and resulting reflow, the prose, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 9 gain a citation in their captions, with minor text reflow; the added bibliography entry also shifts reference-list layout. Figure artwork, table structures, and supplementary visual content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a reference to Moor et al. for the filtration illustrations in Figures 2 and 9, where v1 supplied none, improving attribution and traceability. This is a limited documentation gain; the scientific content, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
